common_name: Red Meidiland Rose (Low Spreading Red Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Red Meidiland is part of the pioneering Meidiland series of low-maintenance landscape roses bred by the French Meilland rose house.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants to allow for a wide, spreading habit. Red Meidiland bears single, five-petaled, bright red flowers with a small white eye at the center, produced in generous clusters over a low, wide, spreading shrub that forms an effective groundcover once established. It blooms in repeated flushes from late spring through fall with little to no deadheading required, and small orange-red hips follow the flowers into fall, adding a further season of interest and a food source for birds. Bred for landscape use rather than cutting, it is tough, disease-resistant, and needs only an annual shaping prune in late winter, making it well suited to banks, slopes, and mass plantings where low maintenance matters most.

common_name: White Meidiland Rose (Low Spreading White Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; White Meidiland is part of the pioneering Meidiland series of low-maintenance landscape roses bred by the French Meilland rose house.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants to allow for a wide, spreading habit. White Meidiland bears large, fully double, pure white flowers on a very low, wide-spreading shrub that forms one of the most effective true groundcover roses in the Meidiland series, hugging the ground more closely than most other landscape roses. It blooms in repeated flushes from late spring through fall with little to no deadheading required, its dense, low habit and glossy foliage providing excellent weed suppression. Bred for landscape use rather than cutting, it is tough, disease-resistant, and needs only an annual shaping prune in late winter, making it a strong choice for banks, slopes, and large-scale mass plantings.

common_name: Pink Meidiland Rose (Single Pink-and-White Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Pink Meidiland is part of the pioneering Meidiland series of low-maintenance landscape roses bred by the French Meilland rose house.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants to allow for a wide, mounding habit. Pink Meidiland bears single, five-petaled flowers combining bright pink outer petals with a white center and golden stamens, a cheerful bicolor pattern produced in large clusters over a bushy, wide-spreading shrub. It blooms in repeated flushes from late spring through fall with little to no deadheading required, and small orange-red hips follow the flowers into fall, extending its ornamental season and feeding birds. Bred for landscape use rather than cutting, it is tough, disease-resistant, and needs only an annual shaping prune in late winter, making it a reliable choice for foundation beds, slopes, and mass plantings.

common_name: Scarlet Meidiland Rose (Vigorous Clustered Scarlet Landscape Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Scarlet Meidiland is part of the pioneering Meidiland series of low-maintenance landscape roses bred by the French Meilland rose house.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants to allow for a large, vigorous, spreading habit. Scarlet Meidiland bears dense clusters of small, semi-double, bright scarlet-red flowers on a vigorous, wide-spreading shrub, one of the larger and more vigorous members of the Meidiland series, well suited to covering a substantial bank or slope. It blooms in repeated flushes from late spring through fall with little to no deadheading required. Bred for landscape use rather than cutting, it is tough, disease-resistant, and needs only an annual shaping prune in late winter, making it a strong choice for erosion control and large-scale mass plantings where a bold red carpet effect is wanted.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, spacing plants to allow for a large, vigorous, spreading habit. Alba Meidiland bears dense clusters of small, fully double, pure white flowers on a vigorous, wide-spreading shrub, one of the more floriferous members of the Meidiland series, capable of covering a substantial bank or slope with a solid carpet of white bloom. It flowers in repeated flushes from late spring through fall with little to no deadheading required. Bred for landscape use rather than cutting, it is tough, disease-resistant, and needs only an annual shaping prune in late winter, making it a strong choice for erosion control, large foundation beds, and mass plantings where minimal upkeep is a priority.
